html:
Nariway Daily Check-in — 2026-08-16

Needs your attention / action today

  • Today is the last prep day before Query A posts tomorrow morning (Mon Aug 17). nariway.com is LIVE with the new identity, that blocker is cleared. What's left: lock Query A's wording, post the first Substack Note so a respondent sees an active publication, ready the interview kit, line up 2–3 warm/direct targets. This is the actual test of everything built so far.
  • Confirm your work-log hours for Aug 14 (~7h) and Aug 15 (~6h), both still logged as draft estimates. One reply keeps the tax record current.
  • Nothing overdue in the CRM. The two nearest scheduled follow-ups (Judith Prowda, Rebecca L. Fine) aren't due until Aug 26.
  • QA: 0 critical this run (down from 1 last week — the case-file field bug is fixed). 4 should-fix items remain, same non-urgent backlog as before, nothing needs you today.

Today I learned

A collection's own tax filing can measure the wrong entity entirely. The Kinsey Collection's public 990 belongs only to a small educational foundation ($649K net assets), while the actual collection is owned and toured by the family's separate for-profit-adjacent enterprise — so a naive reading of that filing (a "1.83x" ratio) describes almost nothing about the real operation's durability. The Thoma Foundation shows the same trap from the other direction: a $1.2B net-assets figure sits on one entity, but until it's confirmed that's the entity actually holding the collection (not a same-family sister foundation), the dataset codes it unknown rather than risk attributing the wrong balance sheet to the wrong case. This matters beyond these two cases — every well-capitalized family foundation in the dataset carries a milder version of the same risk, which means some of the report's most impressive-looking numbers may need a second look before they're charted. Source: report-dataset.md, Pattern 10.

What changed, and what it means

  • nariway.com went LIVE with the new identity. Real progress, per the CFO's read, specifically because it directly unblocks tomorrow's Qwoted post — not because it's another system built.
  • The case dataset jumped from 44 to 47 of 50 — but the more important move was a reconciliation pass, not new coding. The master synthesis file had only ever indexed 24 of 44 coded case files; 20 already-finished cases were sitting uncounted, silently missing from the report's own cross-case patterns. That's fixed now, plus 3 new cases (Credit Suisse/UBS, Pearlman Foundation, Rubin Museum) filled real gaps in the corporate and dispersal typologies.
  • QA's one critical finding is resolved (0 critical this run, down from 1). The 4 remaining should-fix items are unchanged and non-urgent.
  • Both the CFO and CMO stewards flagged the same tension, sharper than last week: two more days went to enrichment — case coding, a board-search shortlist, a QA audit, two new steward agents — with zero client conversations since Dawn. nariway.com going live is the one thing that counts as real progress, because it's what makes tomorrow's post possible.
  • CMO's website watch, with a caveat: search results for nariway.com still surface the old identity. Most likely stale search-index cache (the redeploy is barely two days old), not a reversion — but worth your own eyes on the live site directly since the steward's own fetch tool is blocked from checking it.

Where we stand

Still $0 earned, H7B (will anyone actually pay) still entirely untested. The dataset underneath the flagship report is now genuinely solid — 47 of 50 cases, and this week's reconciliation means the synthesis actually reflects all of them, not just half. None of that is the test, though: tomorrow's Qwoted post is. A response from a stranger, not the post itself, is the only thing that moves the needle toward the million.

Work log

Aug 14 (~7h) and Aug 15 (~6h) are both logged as draft estimates — reply to confirm or correct either.

Brief for the board

Three days running now, the work-log has piled up unconfirmed estimates (Aug 14, 15, and today). A daily ask may be less useful than a single weekly batch to confirm or correct all at once — worth considering if the daily nudge starts feeling like noise rather than a quick reply.
